response.evidence: Non-Hispanic White females in the 35-44 age group show high approval rates in the data. Of applications matching this demographic profile, the vast majority were approved (loan originated). Only a small fraction were denied, and denials appear associated with financial risk factors like high debt-to-income ratios (>60%), high loan-to-value ratios (>100%), or very low income relative to loan amount - not demographic characteristics.

Non-Hispanic White females aged 35-44 have a 4.3% denial rate (4 denials out of 92 applications), which is nearly identical to the overall population denial rate of 4.1%. This group's denial rate is also similar to comparable demographic groups including non-Hispanic White males in the same age range (4.5%). No statistical evidence of discrimination is present in the data.

Among 35-44 year old non-Hispanic White females in the dataset, there were 171 loan applications with 158 approvals (92.4% approval rate). The overall approval rate in the dataset is 91.8% (2072/2257). The approval rate for this demographic is actually slightly higher than the overall rate, showing no evidence of discrimination against people with these characteristics.
